QF.id: Duplicate Share Certificates and Transmission of Securities_8

question.text: A single holder of physical shares passed away without registering any nomination. The sole legal heir is processing transmission. In a no-nomination case, which additional document is required compared to a case where a valid nomination was registered?

answer.text: Notarized affidavit and other requisite documents such as succession certificate, probate of will, or letter of administration, with indemnity
Certified death certificate of the deceased

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 157, where there is no nomination, the legal heir must furnish an affidavit along with other requisite documents such as succession certificate, probate of will, or letter of administration, together with the indemnity. These additional legal documents are not required where a valid nomination exists. The Trap: Original certificates, death certificate, and PAN are required in both scenarios (with and without nomination). The question asks what is additional in a no-nomination case, so only the legal documentation set distinguishes the two processes. Note: Per page 157, relaxed documentation applies to physical securities up to Rs.5 lakhs, allowing a NOC from non-objecting heirs or a notarized family settlement deed with indemnity bond in lieu of the full succession certificate route. Page 168 lists additional low-value transmission documents.
